purpose: External mechanistic anchors for patient-ventilator interaction. Published frequencies are not used as calibration targets for challenge scenarios.

references.study: Chiumello et al., Critical Care Medicine 2007
references.population: 13 mechanically ventilated patients with acute COPD exacerbation
references.mechanism: Flow-cycling criterion in pressure support ventilation
references.published_result: Changing cycling-off from 5% to 40% of peak inspiratory flow reduced cycling delay from 0.40±0.20 to 0.29±0.16 s at PS 5 cmH2O and from 0.93±0.50 to 0.52±0.25 s at PS 15 cmH2O; dynamic PEEPi also decreased.
references.use_in_v017: Directional and scale anchor for delayed-cycling ablation; model challenge is not fit to individual patient data.

references.published_result: External PEEP improved trigger asynchrony but rarely eliminated it completely.
references.use_in_v017: Mechanistic anchor for auto-PEEP threshold loading and external-PEEP unloading.

references.study: de Wit et al., Journal of Critical Care 2009
references.published_result: Ineffective triggering occurred in 17/20 patients, accounted for 88% of asynchronous breaths, and averaged 9±12% of breaths.
references.use_in_v017: Clinical plausibility/context only; the deliberately severe ineffective-trigger challenge is not prevalence-calibrated.

references.published_result: Ventilator rise-time and inspiratory termination settings affect patient-ventilator synchrony.
references.use_in_v017: Supports explicit rise-time and cycling parameters; quantitative fitting deferred.

references.published_result: Double triggering is a recognized asynchrony with potential for breath stacking, overdistension and intrinsic PEEP.
references.use_in_v017: Mechanistic taxonomy and double-trigger event detection.

references.study: Vignaux et al., Intensive Care Medicine 2009
references.published_result: Observed autotriggering, double triggering, ineffective efforts, premature cycling and late cycling; severe asynchrony index >10% was common.
references.use_in_v017: Taxonomy/context only because NIV leak mechanics differ from the current invasive-like forward model.
